For m≥2 the strictly unique maximizer of t^m/(e^t−1) is t_m∈(m−1,m); the dual convex combination α_m f0+(1−α_m)fm≤α_m has only equality radii t=0,t_m, proving all-area upper bound. Two disjoint radial bands with prescribed area weights match α_m A+O_m(A²); single-annulus uniform Lipschitz estimates give e^{−(m!)^(1/m)}A+O_m(A²), strictly worse. Positive strict dual slack implies near-optimal squared-radius area measures weakly converge to p_mδ0+(1−p_m)δ_t_m. At m=1, first-excited Gamma bathtub + f1’=f0−f1 proves exact unique annulus. Independent numerical dual-inequality testing at 5 excitation indices corroborated the analytic argument.
